prerequisites: Solid programming knowledge in the programming language used in the Programming 2 (I) module.

learning_outcomes.text: Students can describe and differentiate essential software paradigms and advanced programming concepts.
Students can apply different software paradigms to solve tasks.
Students can present concrete problem solutions and communicate professionally in discourse with fellow students and teachers.

syllabus_topics: Software paradigms and advanced programming concepts
assessment_rules: The selection of graded and ungraded examination types from the given options is at the discretion of the respective lecturer. The ungraded performance record is provided within the framework of the accompanying internship. The composition of the portfolio examination can be found in the respective valid study regulations. Experimental work: approximately 10 experiments in total. Regular attendance: at least 85% attendance of the event.
bibliography: B. Lahres, G. Rayman, S. Strich, Objektorientierte Programmierung, Rheinwerk Computing
M. Gregoire, Professional C++, John Wiley & Sons
